sections.title: Basic Concept of Profit and Loss
sections.content: Profit occurs when the Selling Price (SP) is more than the Cost Price (CP). Loss occurs when SP is less than CP. Example: If an item costs ₹100 and is sold for ₹120, the profit = ₹20.

sections.title: Profit and Loss in ₹
sections.content: Daily examples: groceries, fruits, school books. ₹-based questions are easier to understand. Example: An item costing ₹200 sold for ₹250 → profit = ₹50.

sections.title: Profit/Loss Percentage
sections.content:
Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100
Loss% = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100
Example: CP = ₹100, SP = ₹120 → Profit% = (20 ÷ 100) × 100 = 20%

sections.title: Important Formulas
sections.content:
1. SP = CP + Profit
2. SP = CP - Loss
3. Profit = SP - CP
4. Loss = CP - SP
5. Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100
6. Loss% = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: Mixing up CP and SP, wrong calculation of profit/loss %, forgetting small ₹ values.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Profit = SP - CP, Loss = CP - SP. Percentage = (Profit/Loss ÷ CP) × 100. ₹ examples make questions easy to solve.

tricks.title: Easy way to calculate 10%
tricks.explanation: Divide the amount by 10 to get 10%.

tricks.title: Quick SP or CP check
tricks.explanation: SP > CP → Profit, SP < CP → Loss

tricks.title: Successive Profit/Loss trick
tricks.explanation: Do not add percentages directly. Calculate stepwise with CP and SP.

tricks.title: Multi-item Profit/Loss trick
tricks.explanation: Find CP and SP of each item separately, then sum up.
tricks.example: Item1: CP ₹50, SP ₹60; Item2: CP ₹100, SP ₹90 → Net Profit = 0
